extra: First $0500 bytes of the mission payload.
Second destination for the mission payload, $3EF0 bytes.

comments.text: Twenty consecutive 64-byte sprite slots in VIC bank $4000. Each slot begins with 21 rows of three pixel bytes, and the last byte is outside the displayed height.
Four sprite slots after the first sixteen mission frames. The VIC slot positions relative to bank $4000 are $A0-$A3.

Four rows of four character codes per 16-byte tile. The map renderer resolves a tile ID through the resident screen-code pointer tables, then indexes this pattern with the character coordinates modulo four.
Upper group of stage tile patterns with IDs $40-$45. IDs $42-$45 occur in the stage maps.
Dictionary slots for tile IDs $46–$85. All sixteen character indices in each slot are zero. The renderer resolves these slots through the same resident pointer tables as the populated patterns.
Dictionary slots for tile IDs $86–$AF. All sixteen character indices in each slot are zero. The renderer resolves these slots through the same resident pointer tables as the populated patterns.
Complete 256-glyph source for the $ADF7 scene. Each glyph occupies eight bytes. The masked wipe at $1E17 reads from this base with an eight-byte stride and writes the corresponding row at $4000.
Tile-indexed colour bytes. The initial playfield renderer at $17CD reads these in parallel with the tile character pointers and $1882 writes the chosen value to colour RAM.
Primary 256-character graphics source. The resident wipe routine at $1DC2 enables RAM under I/O and copies the selected pixel rows to the live character set at $4000.
Rows for character codes $80-$FF in the main stage's 256-glyph set. The masked copy selects them through the same eight-byte stride as the lower codes.
Alternate 256-character graphics source in RAM below the I/O window. The resident wipe routine chooses this source when $1902 is set, unless the alternate scene flag $ADF7 takes priority.
The upper half of the alternate stage's eight-byte character slots, read under CIA and expansion register addresses with I/O banked out.
Stage 1 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 1 grid, 64 entries per row and first 9 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 2 grid, 32 entries per row and first 29 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 2 tile grid from row 30, column 1. The grid has 32 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Two zero-filled rows at the stage-two tile stride of 32 follow the declared grid.
Stage 2 grid, 32 entries per row and first 29 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 2 attribute grid from row 30, column 1. The grid has 32 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Two zero-filled rows at the stage-two attribute stride of 32 follow the declared grid.
Stage 3 grid, 64 entries per row and first 8 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Stage 3 tile grid from row 7, column 36. The grid has 64 cells per row. Each byte supplies a metatile index to the renderer through the stage row pointers.
Stage 3 grid, 64 entries per row and first 8 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 4 grid, 10 entries per row and first 6 rows. Each byte selects one 4 × 4 character tile through the split table at $08D6/$09C6.
Loaded zero bytes between the last declared stage-four tile row and the next stage-four allocation.
Stage 4 grid, 10 entries per row and first 6 rows. The engine uses the low three bits for world-coordinate attribute lookups.
Stage 4 attribute grid from row 7, column 1. The grid has 10 cells per row. Each byte holds the attributes for the matching metatile. The coordinate lookup at $3DFA takes its low three bits.
Copy of the alternate scene's screen codes at $F246–$F2FF. It begins after the stage-four attribute grid and ends before the image that $F811 renders from $F200.
First sixteen rows of the alternate scene image at $F200. Each row contains 64 screen codes. The renderer at $F811 selects a row using the screen row minus the scene origin.
Final eight 64-character rows of the alternate scene image. The last row starts at $F7C0, which the renderer selects when the row difference is 23.
Current coarse horizontal origin of the background.
Current coarse vertical origin of the background.
Column offset for the image copy at $F861.
Vertical origin subtracted from the requested screen row at $F83D.
Direction index selected for the next move. One of four choices indexes $F9A2 and $F996.
Direction used by the fine-scroll update at $FA09.
Counts coarse steps before the direction chooser selects again.
Nonzero enters the exit animation at $F922.
Checked with the first actor's activity byte in the alternate-stage handler at $FB20.
Screen row requested by the alternate-stage image renderer.
Seven loaded bytes following the row index. The final five increase in steps of twelve from $0C through $3C.

For rows below 16, clears 40 screen cells on the offscreen page. Uses the low-byte row difference to select one of 24 64-character rows from $F200 and writes its screen codes while the destination column is below 39.
Low byte of the image row address patched for the indexed load at $F86A.
High byte of the patched row address. The loop writes through the screen pointer in $C8 and stops when X reaches 64.
Fine-scroll positions selected by axis. The move routine changes the selected position modulo 16 and copies its halved value into the VIC scroll workspace.
Number of screen rows drawn for the pending image. The fine-scroll handler waits for this to reach 16 before swapping the screen pages.

Initialises image, scroll, actor and colour fields when $24 is zero. Sets $26, renders a pending image row, advances motion and actor processing, then cycles accent colours. When the exit flag is set, uses the separate exit drawing path.

Disables sprites, updates fine scroll and redraws the scene with shifting image offsets. Waits on two $2B signals before switching pages. When both offset thresholds are reached it sets the stage outcome and background.
Decremented during the alternate scene and divided by four after a modulo-32 mask to select one of eight accent colours.
Eight low three-bit colour values. The caller adds the multicolour flag before drawing the accent.
Four signed coarse or fine steps, -1, +1, -1, +1.
Endpoints $0F and zero for the four motion directions.
Four loaded endpoint values $0F, zero, $0F, zero following the four direction limits.
Four axis indices. Direction 0 or 1 selects the X fields and direction 2 or 3 selects the Y fields.

Waits for the current fine scroll and requested origins to agree. Chooses a new direction when the step counter expires or its limit is reached, changes the requested origin by one and resets the image row counter to redraw the other page.

Changes the chosen axis modulo 16. At the direction endpoint, delays the page flip until the image has rendered 16 rows, then commits the requested origin and rewrites colours. Sets the axis's fine scroll workspace byte.

Immediate zero operand preceding the reset of $F876,Y. When all 16 rows are ready, the alternate path copies the requested row origin to its displayed origin, flips $2E and updates the display scroll nibble.
Loaded zero before the four scene movement bounds at $FA55.
Four origin limits used by the coarse scroll scheduler for left, right, up and down.
Checks $31 for 1 or 2. For either value sets $2C to 1 and clears $27 and $31. Other input values are written back to $31 after subtracting two when it is nonzero.
Sixteen indexed offsets in four runs of four. Used to set colour RAM for the moving background's accent.
Builds a colour RAM base from the current coarse origin and writes the colour in $FA at all sixteen offsets and four extra cells one row apart. Preserves X and Y through its patched load operands.
Immediate operand that restores X, saved by the accent painter at $FA8B.
Immediate operand that restores Y, saved by the accent painter at $FA88.
Returns the coarse vertical origin plus $13 scaled by eight in A.
Calculates eight times the coarse horizontal origin plus $15 as a word in $CA/$CB.
Clears the other two actor Y slots and waits on the scene delay in the specified vertical range. Otherwise generates actor positions relative to the coarse scene origins.
Countdown used by the actor spawn check at $FB0D. Reloads to $64 when $FB16 initializes an actor.

Checks both active projectiles against their screen cells. A character other than space consumes the projectile. A corresponding byte of $0A in the scene plane also plays effects and reduces the remaining target count. On the last target, starts the view transition from the current origin.
Current Y for sprite four. Initialized with $FAD5 plus $20 and moved toward $A8 by the renderer.
Current Y for sprite five. Starts at the same Y as sprite four and moves toward $93.
Two target Y positions, $A8 and $93, indexed by $FC4C for sprite four and sprite five.
Spawn delay for the sprite pair. Counts down at $FBC5 and reloads to $96 when spawning the pair.

Waits for its delay to expire and for both slot-zero Y and the pair active flag to be clear. Seeds both sprite Y positions and the shared X from the view origin helpers, sets the active flag at $F808 and reloads the delay.

For an active pair, disables the resident actor type in slot zero and subtracts two from its 16-bit X. Clears the pair when the resulting X is below ten. Otherwise writes the shared X, advances each nonzero Y by three until its limit and installs both sprite pointers from $0820.

When the contact flag is clear and the pair is active, checks the actor's half-resolution X against the player within six units and requires player Y at least $7A. Sets outcome one and cooldown $17 on contact.
Trailing fragment ends inside a relative branch at the mission metadata boundary. Its two comparisons reuse the horizontal window thresholds $06 and $FA of the preceding contact routine.
The one-based mission number used for this file and for play selection in the resident engine.
Four split pointers with their high bytes at $FCC5. The resident loader at $0B26 selects a stage and gives its grid to the row-pointer builder at $0B46.
High bytes for the tile grids. $0B2B takes the entry for the active stage and puts it in $FC before generating row pointers.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $FCCD. The grid parallels the tile map and the resident coordinate lookup at $3DFA masks each attribute to its low three bits.
High bytes for the attribute grids. $0B35 selects the high byte for $FE.
Stage widths used as a byte stride for the tile and attribute row pointers.
Stage heights used by the resident scaler to derive the vertical playfield limit and by $8EAD to walk the attribute grid.
Indexed stage values copied to $2D during setup by $0AFD.
VIC extended background register $D022 values selected by stage.
VIC extended background register $D023 values selected by stage.
Indexed initial view value written to $1781 before the character drawing loop at $1785.
Four split pointers with high bytes at $FCED. $8FE8 copies 128 bytes from the selected source into a separate workspace half for each player.
High bytes for the placement seeds. $8FF3 selects one for $FC before copying seeds to player workspace.
Indexed stage bytes cached at $0AEA and $0BE0 before display setup.
Stage index compared at $1A82. A match enables the alternate source at $D800 and installs the two operand bytes following this value at $1642/$1643.
Low and high bytes written to $1642/$1643 on the stage selected by $FCF5.
High byte of the alternate stage callback address copied into the resident call at $1641.
Four stage-indexed masks copied to $1901 at $0B11. The resident sprite routines AND their priority bits with this mask before writing VIC register $D01B.
The pair at $FCFC/$FCFD supplies the two operand bytes at $2B0A/$2B0B.
High byte of the pair installed at $2B0A/$2B0B.
Low and high bytes of the mission-provided routine that $1AB3 calls after preparing the stage grids.
High byte of the stage setup call target, installed at $1AB5.
Forty-eight loaded zero bytes between the stage hook directory and the shared bytes at $FD30.

A copy of the sixteen default C64 KERNAL RAM vectors at $0314–$0333. The entries begin with the IRQ, BRK and NMI targets $EA31, $FE66 and $FE47, followed by the BASIC and device I/O hooks. All five mission payloads carry the same copy.
Forty-eight loaded zero bytes between the shared bytes at $FD30 and the stage placement source at $FD80.

Stage 1 placement seed copied into player workspace by $8FE8. A record has a destination low byte, destination high byte and value. A zero value ends the loop that applies records to the working stage grid.
Stage 2 placement seed copied into page $0200. The resident setup applies the value of each record at its two-byte destination and stops at the first zero value.

Placement records shared by stages 3 and 4 in this mission, with an in-game destination word followed by a value byte. The loader supplies $70 bytes of this workspace source before the overlay ends at $FEEF.
